q: Which one is a gravity wall?
n: Figure A is a gravity wall that resists by its own mass.

q: Which one is an anchored wall?
n: Figure E is held back by a tieback anchor.

q: Which one is a buttress wall?
n: Figure D has its ribs on the exposed face: a buttress wall.

q: Which one is a counterfort wall?
n: Figure C has its ribs buried in the backfill: a counterfort wall.

q: Where is the ideal location for placing a shear wall?
n: Shear walls are best placed around elevator and stair cores.

q: What is a shear wall mainly for?
n: Shear walls resist wind and quakes.

q: What is the compressive strength of non-load-bearing concrete hollow blocks (CHB)?
n: Non-load-bearing CHB is about 350 psi.

q: What is the compressive strength of load-bearing concrete hollow blocks (CHB)?
n: Load-bearing CHB is about 700 psi.

q: What is added inside hollow blocks to raise their load capacity?
n: Reinforced, grouted cells.

q: What is the minimum thickness of a load bearing CHB (Concrete Hollow Block) available in the Philippines?
n: Load-bearing CHB starts at 150 mm.

q: What horizontal member in a framed wall gives lateral support to the wall panels?
n: Girts span between columns.

q: What is the maximum spacing between stiffener columns in an ordinary CHB wall?
n: Stiffener columns are spaced at about 3 m.

q: A stiffener beam is required for a CHB wall if the wall height exceeds how many meters?
n: Per the MST answer key: 3meters.

q: In CHB walls, at what spacing are horizontal reinforcing bars normally placed?
n: Fajardo's CHB method places horizontal bars at every 3 layers of blocks.

q: What is the minimum size of reinforcing bars required for a 3-meter-high wall?
n: Per the MST answer key: 10 mm diameter.

q: What is the typical size of reinforcing bars used for an 8-inch concrete hollow block (CHB) wall?
n: 8-inch CHB walls take 12 mm bars.

q: What is the minimum CHB thickness for non-load-bearing walls?
n: 4-in. CHB.

q: What is the minimum CHB thickness for load-bearing walls?
n: Load-bearing CHB walls need at least 150 mm.

q: What wall holds back earth between different ground levels?
n: Retaining wall.

q: What is the most common type of failure in a retaining wall?
n: Per the MST answer key: Failure at the moment arm.

q: What element at the base of a retaining wall adds stability?
n: The heel and toe resist overturning.

q: What is provided through a retaining wall to relieve water pressure?
n: Weep holes drain the backfill.

q: Which condition is most dangerous for a shear wall?
n: Openings cut its stiffness.

q: Where do shear walls rest?
n: They continue to the foundation.

q: For seismic reasons, where should the core walls go in a 15-storey building 15 m wide and 25 m long?
n: A central core limits torsion.

q: Which wall is designed to resist lateral forces in its own plane?
n: Shear walls act in-plane.

q: What boundary element of a diaphragm or shear wall resists axial stress?
n: Chords take tension and compression.

q: What is the nominal thickness of a concrete hollow block (CHB) for an exterior wall without plastering?
n: Exterior unplastered CHB walls are 150 mm.

q: Which of the following is NOT a standard thickness for a CHB?
n: CHB come in 4, 6 and 8 in; 10 in is not standard.

q: Which of the following is NOT a commonly used CHB thickness?
n: 5 in is not a common CHB thickness.

q: Brick masonry is weak in:
n: Masonry is strong only in compression.

q: How many CHB units are required for a wall measuring 10.2 meters in length and 3.3 meters in height, excluding a 300 mm lintel beam and 300 mm wide stiffener column? Include a 5% contingency allowance.
n: Net area = (10.2 − 0.3) × (3.3 − 0.3) = 29.7 m²; at 12.5 CHB per m², that is 371.3; plus 5% = 389.8, or about 388.

q: Horizontal bars used in CHB walls are typically installed at what spacing?
n: Per the MST answer key: 600 mm every 3 layers.

q: What is the standard spacing for vertical reinforcement in a CHB wall?
n: Vertical bars in CHB walls are typically 0.60 m apart.

q: What bar size is recommended for a 4-in. CHB wall?
n: 10 mm bars.
